items.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant Interview, 1962-05-17
items.q: Papa Celisna said, she don't fool somebody else. She said, but I'll be there... Papa Celisna began playing... They really, really did put it on that night. We really had a wonderful concert.

ctx.x: I'd like to ask you about that very first year. What kind of music did you have when you said it was in Congo Square with some people called Borrigan?

What kind of music we had? We had Papa Salastare himself with Lizzie Miles singing. We had the best. The people start from the bottom up, but we had the best first. We had the best first. We've never had a concert like that since. But he donated his time. Well, I tell you how we got this Beauregard Square. Congo Square. I will call it Congo Square because I knew it by Congo Square. The Pops concert was going on. You know about the Pops concert. And so I went to see the mayor to ask for this square. And he was…
Bill Bailey, once the piece come over.

items.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant Interview, 1962-05-17
items.q: Well, there was a white group who followed Papa Celeste everywhere he went... They just liked his music.

ctx.x: You know, the youngsters claim that they are going head over here for rock and roll. But some of our members bring their children and their grandchildren and give them invitations to our ball. And I noticed they enjoy themselves mighty well with that Dixieland music. Oh, more than their own dances. And they come every year. Yes, indeed. So they enjoy it, but I guess because rock and roll has taken over so much, they think they like it best. But actually, I think deep down in them, they like them for Dixieland.…

Well, there was a white group who followed Papa Celeste everywhere he went. He'd go to Baton Rouge. There would be a bus load there with them. I don't know where they were from. They were from Tulane or where. Don't you remember when he went out there for the concert? Oh, about 15 or 20, even more, following him, wherever he'd go. He'd go and really have him to go out there at this concert he was giving. And we saw that whole bus load of young white girls and boys. And they told me they followed him everywhere he…
You know, we haven't hardly talked to you at all. The ladies are keeping you quiet over there.
